linux_cohost_feasibility.scope: Existing native Gameplay hostfxr route called from an already-running managed process; native entity service is a small deterministic callback. No Avalonia, Windows, full runtime physics, or cross-version compatibility qualification.

failures_and_corrections.detail: An unmanaged Python host used hostfxr from the flat self-contained editor directory, which lacked an installed shared framework layout. The native harness was rerun with the installed matching hostfxr. The actual already-running editor separately passed with its bundled hostfxr.

The first interpreter lacked Pillow; an existing interpreter with Pillow was used. The first fixture report was inside the project and correctly rejected; the test separated its project and report directories before rerunning.
Opening the first Gameplay window attempted to attach advanced fields to two visual parents. Each control now belongs to one row. The corrected final package passed both GUI suites.
Applying live values could discard an independently edited reload path. Apply now preserves that draft; explicit Refresh or successful Reload resets it. The final GUI suite asserts preservation.

limitations: The profile is session-local; no persistent project launch profile, source watcher or background compiler is supplied.
CoreCLR/bridge selection is process-lived. The supported Game<TState> SDK remains bounded; arbitrary per-entity scripts or whole-engine hot reload are not implemented.
All Windows GUI input was semantic/scripted, not physical keyboard/mouse/IME or broad accessibility qualification.
Windows was locked. Avalonia visual-content PNGs qualify this retained layout only, not an OS screenshot, native title bar, display/compositor, or physical interaction.
The native Game viewport BMP is distinct from UI-content rendering. No new graphics quality or performance benchmark is claimed.
Linux cohosting is a small native shim fixture, not a Linux editor. Console and clean-machine deployment remain unqualified.
No hosted CI ran. These are small local correctness and lifecycle fixtures, not production workload or sustained memory/frame-time measurements.
